c0-frame.title: Frame cycle 2 as shotgun on the graph's nature
c0-frame.imperative: Flavor shotgun (human-picked). The target: the NATURE of the graph itself. Inspiration sits somewhere between a mind map and Wikipedia; the human wants to poke at whether other organizing forms (graph or not-graph) should be on the table. Three research excursions carry the cycle; divergence folds their findings plus agent one-liners at consolidation.
c0-frame.result: framed: shotgun on graph nature, 3 research excursions (human-initiated)

q1-graph-nature.title: What IS the thing we're building - is 'graph' even the right form?
q1-graph-nature.imperative: The cycle's point question. The mind-map-to-Wikipedia spectrum is the stated inspiration; the excursions test whether that spectrum is the whole space. Fold excursion findings and any agent divergence here; the finding is a sharpened statement of the form (or a widened candidate set).
q1-graph-nature.finding: The graph survives as the form, but the survey reframes the question: almost every organizing form ENCODES as a graph, almost none are WELL SERVED by the encoding - the informative question is which invariant the encoding stops enforcing. Four invariants need explicit homes in our design: (1) the un-named relation (Aquanet evidence: force typing and authors stop linking); (2) the computed relation (guard fields: relevance as a read-time predicate over task state - rhymes with the dial); (3) scope (true-in-context-C, not globally down-weighted); (4) content-addressed entry co-equal with traversal (Codd: navigational models lose on ease of use). Genuinely non-graph survivors: conceptual spaces / embedding geometry (similarity needs no authoring; VSA shows graph-vs-vector is a false binary) and retrieval-outcome scheduling (orthogonal to topology; answers where weights come from). SCOPED: mind-map-to-Wikipedia spectrum plus adjacent traditions searched; sheaf-theoretic KR, TDA, non-Western traditions, archival/legal/process notations NOT searched (listed in x1-result).

x1-organizing-forms.title: Excursion: other forms for organizing diverse thoughts (beyond graphs?)
x1-organizing-forms.imperative: Research excursion, human-initiated. One named question: what ways/tools have people used to organize diverse interconnected thoughts, and is there anything that is NOT a graph? Brief at excursions/x1-brief.md, recorded on the board. Dispatch background via run_crew.py (external backend); result at excursions/x1-result.md. Scoped nulls apply.
x1-organizing-forms.finding: 24-form cited survey. Headline: graphs are expressively universal in an uninteresting way; per-form the question is what the reduction loses. Three recurring losses: enforced axis independence, the un-named relation, the computed relation. Shortlist challenging node-and-edge: conceptual spaces/embeddings, guard-field suppression, faceted/OLAP roll-up, retrieval-outcome scheduling, scope+reified relations (trails as first-class paths). Steals: red link/empty slot, Novak proposition test, migration-as-forgetting, IBIS type restraint, stable human-legible IDs. Warnings: Woods 1975 (typed edges need stated semantics), Codd (traversal must not be the only access path). SCOPED NULL: no mature non-graph-encodable tool found; traditions not searched are listed in the result.

x2-two-speed-memory.title: Excursion: two-speed graph vs working/long-term memory architectures
x2-two-speed-memory.imperative: Research excursion, human-initiated. One named question: how do working-memory vs long-term-memory architectures (cognitive science AND software/AI systems) handle fast-sloppy capture and consolidation/promotion, and what should the two-speed graph steal? Brief at excursions/x2-brief.md. Dispatch background via run_crew.py (external backend); result at excursions/x2-result.md. Scoped nulls apply.
x2-two-speed-memory.finding: Two-speed split independently reinvented by brains (CLS), storage engines (LSM), and agent frameworks - the shape is sound. BUT our proposed merge-up variant (unconditional, end-of-task, rewrite-in-place, episode-compressing) is the exact configuration Zhang 2026 empirically kills (100%->54% on ARC-AGI after consolidating from ground truth; drift toward the model's prior). Survives: gated + additive + episode-preserving. Five steals: competitive gating at eviction (W-TinyLFU), online eligibility tagging during the task (ripples / importance-at-write), bi-temporal supersede-never-delete (Zep), keep raw episodes permanently (promotion = copy-that-abstracts), atomic units with first-class NOOP verb (Mem0). Structural challenges: end-of-task trigger is an assumption NO surveyed system shares (impasse-resolved is the unexplored best fit); hard two-store split contestable (Cowan / generative-agents: one store with activation marking). Authority: best systems split deciding from executing. SCOPED NULL: kills unconditional rewrite-in-place merge-up only; the two-speed concept stands.

x3-linking-heuristics.title: Excursion: cognitive rules (like 'ask why 5 times') for building conceptual links
x3-linking-heuristics.imperative: Research excursion, human-initiated. One named question: what elicitation rules / cognitive techniques in the '5 whys' family exist for deliberately building conceptual links, and which could an agent run mechanically to grow graph edges? Brief at excursions/x3-brief.md. Dispatch background via run_crew.py (external backend); result at excursions/x3-result.md. Scoped nulls apply.
x3-linking-heuristics.finding: 24-technique cited catalog across six traditions. Two design-relevant distinctions the literature lacks: edge-only vs node-minting rules, and checkable vs unfalsifiable output. Build-first shortlist: Ahrens four-way relate check (contradict/correct/support/extend, mints nothing, falsifiable), Idea Compass (4 typed edges per call incl. rare contrast edges), bounded causal descent (5 Whys depth-capped at 3 + Ishikawa fan, bind-or-mint), TRIZ trade-off detection (sole source of trades-off-against), structure-mapped analogy with systematicity scoring (only analogy rule with a ranking criterion; feeds schema-minting). Free: Novak cross-link ranker (prefer distant endpoints; graph query, no model call). Edge-refinement category discovered: Toulmin warrant-naming upgrades existing edges. SCOPED NULLS: random pairing (PO, Oblique Strategies) and SCAMPER fail as AUTONOMOUS rules (LLM relates anything on request, no truth condition) - revive with human-in-loop or a downstream usefulness signal. Caveat: human generation-effects do not transfer; judge rules on edge yield only.

consolidation: Cycle 2 poked at the graph's nature via three parallel research excursions; all returned, registry-verified. CONSOLIDATED PICTURE: (1) The graph survives the widest survey we could throw at it - no mature non-graph tool exists - but the survey converts 'is it a graph?' into 'which invariants does node-and-edge fail to enforce, and where do they live in our design?' Four need homes: un-named/provisional relations, computed (task-state-conditional) relations, scoped truth, and content-addressed entry co-equal with traversal. (2) The two-speed candidate is REVISED, not culled: the shape is triply-confirmed prior art, but merge-up must become gated/competitive, additive (supersede, never rewrite; keep episodes permanently), with eligibility tagged during the task; the end-of-task trigger and the hard two-store split are demoted from assumptions to open questions. (3) Rule-driven edge growth is a NEW candidate with a concrete build-first shortlist of five falsifiable-ish rules and two hard autonomous nulls. (4) Cross-synthesis: guard-field suppression is a rival/complement mechanization of the dial; the unnamed-relation problem and the working graph may solve each other (fast tier holds untyped association, merge-up is the naming step); one 'usefulness signal' (did a surfaced edge get used?) unlocks learned pull, wild-linking rules, and promotion gating simultaneously. Board updated: 3 new candidates, 5 new open threads, cycle-2 findings section. NOT converged - the human's call.
